clue.text: Second-hand stalls quick to accept a bit of foreign money

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the word for quick holds the money phrase inside it

parts.note: fleet means fast or quick
taken as written
the mark was the German currency

explanation.surface: A second-hand market where traders are eager to take a coin or two in foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' reads as describing the stallholders, but it is the outer word. The mark was Germany's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is an open market of stalls selling used goods and bric-a-brac.

clue.text: Bar establishment where president drank?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the Inns of Court, the institutions of the legal Bar in London

definitions.note: a whimsical reading of the name as a president's pub
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: read literally, the tavern belonging to Abraham Lincoln

explanation.walkthrough: The Bar is the body of barristers; the four Inns of Court in London train and admit them, and one shares its name with Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the four Inns of Court, the professional bodies to which every English barrister belongs.

clue.text: An attraction designed, we hear, to be used in moderation

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is to be judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a lure that was intended: bait is an attraction, meant is designed

explanation.surface: Something tempting is said to be intended for use in moderation.
explanation.definitionFit: Abatement is a lessening or easing, so it is a near synonym of moderation.

clue.text: Witnesses present for trials

parts.note: at as in present at a meeting
tests are trials

explanation.surface: People who saw a crime are there to give evidence in court cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witnesses' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to or certify something, so witnesses as a verb matches.

clue.text: Type needs alteration in suit — nice quality!

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the word for the card suit

parts.note: hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

indicators.note: an alteration is a change, so the word it governs has its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone needs their suit altered, and the tailor's obliging manner is praised as a nice quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing being tailored, but it is the card suit; 'Type' is not the definition but the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kind-hearted, warm and generous towards others, is a pleasant trait of character, so a nice quality.

clue.text: Counter-reformation's slaughter

indicators.note: reformation means forming again, so the letters are made into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The killing that went on during the Catholic Counter-Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated Counter-Reformation looks like one historical term, but it splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter an opponent in sport is to defeat them heavily, which is what trounce means.

clue.text: Placid learner put in academic stream

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A calm student set to study at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid and calm are synonyms describing a peaceful, untroubled state.

clue.text: Foreign friend one's naming? No, all names withheld

indicators.note: N is short for name, so withholding all names means every N is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asked to name a friend refuses, keeping every name back.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a friend, used in English for a pal.

clue.text: Live under a tree, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it as the letters run downwards

parts.note: may is the hawthorn tree
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Perhaps one could make a home beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece under another comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are both adverbs expressing possibility rather than certainty.

clue.text: Remove lead from slow opponents at cards?

definitions.note: a phrase meaning to free, as when a dog's lead is undone

parts.note: not fast, so slow
in bridge, East and North sit on opposing sides

explanation.surface: Someone wants to take the lead away from sluggish card players.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North partners South and East partners West, so East and North are opponents. 'Lead' looks like a card-game term but is a dog's leash.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a dog's leash is to undo or release the fastening, taking the lead off.

clue.text: Something strange seen in every quarter of 1997

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a peculiar thing or curiosity

definitions.note: a playful description: each of the four digits is odd
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: a four-digit year splits into four quarters of one digit each, and 1, 9, 9 and 7 are all odd numbers

explanation.surface: Something peculiar keeps cropping up throughout the year, quarter after quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter of a four-digit number is one digit; every digit of 1997 is odd, so oddness is found in each quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is a strange or peculiar thing, so the noun phrase defines it directly.

clue.text: Mischievous spirits not welcomed on course

definitions.meaning: second meaning: golf scores of one over par, unwelcome to a golfer

explanation.surface: Troublesome ghosts are unwelcome on a racecourse or golf links.
explanation.walkthrough: On a golf course a bogey is a hole played in one stroke over par.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogey is both a mischievous goblin of folklore and a golf score of one stroke over par.

clue.text: Applause not all found attractive

parts.note: as in giving someone a big hand
some is a part rather than the whole

explanation.surface: Not everyone in the audience clapped, yet the performance was found attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome describes a good-looking person, a synonym of attractive in appearance.

clue.text: Claim ritual must be changed, involving all sorts of people

indicators.note: being changed means the words are put into a different order of letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone argues a ceremony should be reformed to include everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiracial describes something including people of many different ethnic backgrounds.

clue.text: As soon as Conservative splits unity

indicators.note: something that splits a word goes into its middle, dividing it in two

parts.note: unity is the number one
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory politician immediately breaks up party unity.
explanation.definitionFit: Once can be a conjunction meaning as soon as, as in 'once he arrives, we eat'.

clue.text: Outrageously rubbish half my clues (but not first in crossword)

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to wreck, so the letters are thrown into disorder
but not tells us one letter is left out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A setter confesses, with mock outrage, that half the clues are rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like the definition or a noun, but it is the anagram signal; remove the C from the fodder first.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefully and outrageously both describe behaviour that is disgraceful and deserves condemnation.

clue.text: One hunts king out thus?

indicators.note: out suggests disorder or being put wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Is this how a person chases a monarch off the throne?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: hunting a king out is deposing him.
explanation.definitionFit: To unthrone is to remove a monarch from power, which is what driving a king out does.

clue.text: Sweet teacher expert at making money

parts.note: a mint is a sweet
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: A sweet-natured teacher who is good at earning cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making money' sounds like earning but means literally manufacturing coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A mintmaster is the official in charge of a mint, where coins are literally manufactured.

clue.text: Ways gunmen raised the equipment they need

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means writing upwards, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: lanes are ways or roads
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Armed men set up the routes and kit they require.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment of gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons and ammunition, what gunmen need to fight.

clue.text: Soothing the others if you reveal only the conclusions

parts.note: the rest are the others

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so only the final letter of each word is kept

parts.note: end letters of these two words
end letter of this word

explanation.surface: Telling others only how things end can be calming.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful describes something calming and peaceful, a synonym of soothing.

clue.text: Cut spruce

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to clip or shorten
second meaning: neat and smart in appearance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the tree being felled, but it is the adjective meaning neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim is a verb for clipping something shorter and an adjective for neat, tidy smartness.

clue.text: Girl was thoughtful and not diverted

parts.note: a girl's name
to muse is to ponder

explanation.surface: A girl sat lost in thought and did not find it entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverted here means entertained or amused, so not diverted describes someone left unentertained.

clue.text: Having no facets complete?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gemstone not yet shaped by a cutter
second meaning: a film or book shown in full, unedited

explanation.surface: Is something without any facets simply whole?
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut diamond has no polished facets, and an uncut film or text is complete and unabridged.

clue.text: Forging equipment found in Italian village

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Blacksmith's gear discovered in a small Italian community.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block on which a smith hammers metal when forging.

clue.text: Run without a stitch

parts.note: surface reading: knitting or tights, a ladder in fabric that no stitch holds
setter's reading: dash about without a stitch of clothing on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' and 'stitch' suggest knitting or hosiery; 'without a stitch' means naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, often a sports ground, as a prank.

clue.text: Warning home appears to collapse

parts.note: Latin for beware, old schoolboy slang for a lookout's warning
being in is being at home

explanation.surface: A warning is issued because the house looks ready to fall down.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE, pronounced 'kay-vee', was the cry British schoolboys used to warn that a teacher was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is to fall inwards or give way, a phrasal verb meaning the same as collapse.

clue.text: Object is found by English females men respected in Turkey

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
F for female, doubled for the plural
an end is an aim or object
taken as written

explanation.surface: An item turns up alongside some Englishwomen, and Turkish dignitaries respect them.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi is a Turkish title of respect for a man of education or standing, like 'sir'.

clue.text: Attack with hammer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a charge with a lance
second meaning: a ... hammer, a heavy pivoted forge hammer

explanation.surface: Someone goes on the offensive wielding a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilt is a jousting thrust or attack, and also a heavy forge hammer raised on a pivot.

clue.text: On an even keel, but without energy?

definitions.note: read cryptically as list-less-ly, without any list or lean
definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsical: a ship with no list sails upright
second meaning: in a lethargic, apathetic way

explanation.surface: A boat sails steadily level, though somehow lacking any drive.
explanation.walkthrough: A list is a ship's lean to one side, so a ship on an even keel moves without list.
explanation.definitionFit: Listlessly means in a languid, apathetic manner, lacking vigour or enthusiasm.
